sam.t: Heads up — after the http2->gRPC framing rewrite in ingress-proxy we see an extra ~8-12ms p50 on small requests (1-8 tokens). Noticed higher CPU on host side. Perf attached below.

pranay: Can you paste the perf flame or a breakdown? Is this tokenization, request parsing, or gRPC unboxing?

sam.t: Here are the hotspot percentages from a 30s perf sample on canary nodes:
```
parse_request_handle()        38%
  -> grpc_unbox_frame()       12%
  -> request_tokenize()       27%
  -> socket_writev()          15%
memcpy + boundary checks       8%
syscall overhead (write)       6%
```
Seems like tokenization + extra small writev calls after the rewrite. write syscalls per request jumped 7 -> 21 on median.

ira: That matches my quick diff — we added an extra per-frame boundary check in the new grpc framing code (PR #1842, sha: f3a1b2c). It avoids a rare bug but introduced an extra memcpy and per-frame decision.

deploy-bot: deploy: Canary rollout of ingress-proto v2 (f3a1b2c) paused due to performance regression.

maria: Two suspects: 1) fragmentation increased so more small frames get passed to runtime (syscall/writev cost). 2) kernel selection could be falling back — small-request patterns may prefer a different execution path and we're losing quantized fastpath.

sam.t: Agreed. Quick numbers: small requests hitting non-quantized path rose from 4% -> 31% on the canary. Batcher seen that expected batching heuristics no longer group these tiny frames because they arrive as multiple micro-frames.

pranay: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- coalesce small frames in host-proxy before handing to runtime (cheap fix)
- remove redundant memcpy/boundary checks by checking a length prefix once per call rather than per frame
- add an upstream batcher hint so the runtime preserves kernel selection for tiny requests (force the quantized fastpath when payload < X bytes)

ira: I'm working on a micro-patch to coalesce frames and drop the extra memcpy; running local microbench now. Also will run KV cache warmup tests — if fragmentation changes request shapes, cache miss rate can spike and amplify latency.

maria: Can we also add a short perf regression test in CI that simulates 1-8 token requests with streaming chunking? If we catch this earlier we avoid future rollouts.

sam.t: Good plan. I attached a sample reproduction harness command: `./bench/ingress_smallreq -mode=grpc -frames=rand_small -qps=500 -duration=30s`. Results before patch: p50=22ms, after rewrite p50=31ms. After local coalesce patch (wip) I'm seeing p50 drop back to ~24ms.

pranay: Once ira's patch lands, I'll add a quick kernel-selection assertion in our perf-suite: assert quantized_path_rate >= 90% for tiny-request profile. If it drops we fail the job.

maria: Logging todo: add metrics for writev_count/request, frames_per_request, and kv_cache_miss_rate at the ingress boundary so we can attribute regressions automatically. Also link this thread to perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.dev/d/ingress/small-reqs (tracking)

ira: Patch pushed to canary branch, running canary smoke. Will post results in ~30m.

sam.t: Thanks — I'll stand by with rollback plan if we see >5ms p50 regression on production canaries. :thumbsup:
